speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing jaundice, itching, weight loss, pale stools, and dark urine; to determine the underlying cause, please tell me your age, sex, and how long these symptoms have been present.

speaker: Patient
text: 72-year-old male. The patient has experienced gradual yellow discoloration of the skin and generalized pruritus over the past 2 weeks. He also reports a decreased appetite and a weight loss of 6.3 kg (14 lb). The patient’s stool has been pale, and his urine is very dark. Three years ago, he had an episode of acute upper abdominal pain, which was managed with IV fluids, NSAIDs, and dietary modification. The patient has abstained from alcohol for these three years, after having consumed 1–2 beers daily for 40 year...

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your age, weight loss, pale stools, and dark urine, we must evaluate for pancreatic or biliary obstruction. Can you describe the location and severity of any current abdominal pain? REQUEST TEST: Liver Function Panel; REQUEST TEST: Abdominal Ultrasound.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Temperature: Normal, Blood Pressure: Normal, Heart Rate: Normal, Respiratory Rate: Normal; Abdominal Examination: Inspection shows Jaundice noted in the conjunctivae and skin, Auscultation shows Bowel sounds normal, Percussion shows Abdomen is soft, non-distended, Palpation shows No tenderness, but a soft, cystic mass palpated in the right upper quadrant; Serum Studies: Bilirubin_Total: 5.6 mg/dL, Direct_Bilirubin: 4.8 mg/dL, Alkaline_Phosphatase: 192 U/L, AST: 32 U/L, ALT: 34 U/L; Abdominal_Ultrasonography: Anechoic cystic mass in the subhepatic region. Dilation of the intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Choledocholithiasis (common bile duct stone) causing obstructive jaundice.

The ultrasound shows a cystic mass and dilated bile ducts with high direct bilirubin, but the "soft, cystic mass" in the RUQ could be a gallbladder remnant or a stone impacted in the CBD; given your history of upper abdominal pain three years ago and current signs of biliary obstruction, this is the most likely cause. Would you like me to order an MRCP or Endoscopic Ultrasound (EUS) to confirm the presence of a stone versus a cystic lesion like a choledochal cyst?
